svg.text: Le Chatelier's principle: a disturbed equilibrium shifts to undo the disturbance

g.text: add BiCl3 or water: shifts right, more white BiOCl precipitate and HCl
add BiOCl or HCl: shifts left, precipitate dissolves, more BiCl3
remove BiCl3: shifts left; remove BiOCl or HCl: shifts right
a new equilibrium position is reached each time, but Kc is unchanged
(Kc = [BiOCl][HCl]^2 / [BiCl3][H2O] as printed)

svg.text: Pressure or volume: N2 + 3H2 gives 2NH3 (4 moles to 2)

g.text: raise the pressure (shrink the volume): shifts to the side with fewer gas moles,
forward, more ammonia; lower the pressure: shifts to more moles, reverse
no effect when no gases are involved or when gas moles are equal
(H2 + I2 gives 2HI; CO + H2O gives CO2 + H2)
the equilibrium position moves, Kc does not

svg.text: Temperature: the only factor that changes Kc

g.text: exothermic 2SO2 + O2 gives 2SO3, delta H = -198 kJ:
heating shifts left, less SO3, Kc falls (2.8 x 10^2 at 1000 K; 1 x 10^26 at 298 K);
cooling shifts right, more SO3
endothermic N2O4 gives 2NO2, delta H = +57.2 kJ:
heating shifts right, more brown NO2, Kc rises (7.7 x 10^-5 at 273 K; 0.4 at 373 K);
cooling shifts left, more colourless N2O4
rule: adding heat favours the direction that absorbs heat

svg.text: Catalyst: faster to equilibrium, same position (Figure 8.3)
both forward and reverse barriers fall; the yield at equilibrium is unchanged
Position of equilibrium against equilibrium constant

g.text: position of equilibrium: the relative amounts of products and reactants in the mixture; shifted right means more products
concentration, pressure and volume move the position but leave Kc alone; temperature moves both; a catalyst moves neither
Kc does not depend on the starting concentrations; equilibrium can be approached from either side; pure solids and liquids
are omitted from Kc; the state must be reversible and the vessel closed
